Dupont Garden

PhysicsCurvesCoordinates
Game: This is a fountain, not a game: jets of water jump up and fall down, and there is nothing to win.
How to play: Press Run to send the jets up and Stop to pause. Change Drops, Delay or the pattern, then drag dots A and B along a curve to read its height.
Look for the math

The page calls this an animated demonstration of projectile trajectory. Its exact claim is: By 1604 he concluded that projectiles travel along parabolic trajectories. Every jet drawn by the applet was checked against that statement, and it holds for all of them.

Two motions at once

Galileo's idea was to split the motion into two independent parts. A jet moves sideways at a steady speed: x(t) = X0 + Vt. At the same time gravity pulls it down: y(t) = Wt − 9.8t²/2. Changing V changes where it lands but leaves y(t) alone. Here projectile motion is measured in the applet's own units, with g = 9.8.

Why the curve is a parabola

Eliminate the time t from the two formulas. From the first one, t = (x − X0)/V; put that into the second:

y = (W/V)(x − X0) − (4.9/V²)(x − X0)²

That is a quadratic in x, so the path is a parabola. The highest point comes halfway through the flight, at t = W/9.8, and reaches W²/19.6. The jet is back at ground level at t = 2W/9.8, having travelled 2VW/9.8 sideways. A logic test checked those formulas and the constant downward acceleration over a grid of launches; it also found that the applet's own jets always have V ≠ 0, so none of their paths is a straight vertical line. Parabolas are one kind of conic section, the family Kepler used for the differently shaped orbits mentioned on the original page.

Inside the fountain

The applet builds six patterns: ten random jets, twenty random jets, and slow or fast flights across the picture in either direction. Before each pattern it scales the upward speed so the jets fit the frame; then each jet drops a small bead every half unit of time. Run picks one of the six patterns at random and starts a new one when every jet has landed. Drops runs from 1 to 50 and Delay from 10 to 1000 milliseconds, just as in the original. The two dots here are reading probes: they snap to the current curve and show the height, but they never change the water.

Try Slow, left to right with one drop and move A and B: the beads are further apart in time, so you can see that equal time steps give equal sideways steps but unequal changes in height.

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
